question: What is the standard chessboard size in tournament play (in terms of rows and columns)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**8x8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **standard chessboard size** used in tournament play consists of **8 rows** (ranks) and **8 columns** (files), forming a total of **64 squares**. This is the internationally accepted standard.
 
• The chessboard alternates between **light and dark squares**, ensuring clear visibility of moves during play.
 
• Each square measures roughly **2 inches on each side** in competitive setups to accommodate standard chess pieces.
 
• The chessboard is labeled with **letters (A to H)** for columns and **numbers (1 to 8)** for rows, aiding players in identifying positions.
